conviction_note: The company's own Q2 guide (NIM up a couple of bp, nonint expense $24.0-24.8M, nonint income $3.8-4.1M, mid-single-digit H2 loan growth) arithmetically implies Q3 EPS near $1.55-1.57 against a $1.50-1.51 consensus, a ~3% beat. That fits this name's habit of beating by 2-7 cents, and the last three beats of that size traded -3.26%, -1.39% and +0.63%, so the fundamental read (+3%) and the reaction read (p_up 52 on a 2.6% absolute move, +0.10) are allowed to diverge. impact_sum (+0.55) is larger than the scaled number because each small positive is sized on its own and no single one decides the print.
bar: Q3 2026 diluted EPS consensus $1.51 (Earnings Whispers, revenue est $40.17M, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/HBCP) and $1.50 (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/HBCP/earnings/). The two sources agree to a cent; three analysts (Zacks count via AP, https://wtop.com/news/2026/07/home-bancorp-q2-earnings-snapshot/). Company gives no numeric EPS guide, only line-item guidance on the Q2 call (Benzinga transcript, https://www.webull.com/news/15267258756637696).
positioning_check: Short interest 311,849 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement (down from 319,323 on 09-15), 4.0% of 7.87M shares outstanding, 4.5 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/hbcp/shortinterest, read 2026-10-19). It roughly tripled from 104,632 on 2026-03-13. Moderate, not crowded. No usable option chain (baseline options.status no_paired_strikes), so no skew and no priced direction. Tape: spot $65.90 at 12:00 ET, -3.27% over 20 days, -9.1% from the 52-week high, 20-day realised vol 13.7%.

findings.finding: Management's own Q2-call line items (NIM up 'a couple of basis points' in Q3, noninterest expense $24.0-24.8M, noninterest income $3.8-4.1M, mid-single-digit H2 loan growth off a Q2 base of $35.8M NII, 4.24% NIM and $2.78B loans) imply roughly $36.5M NII, $15.2M pretax and EPS near $1.55-1.57 at Q2's ~19% tax rate and 7.84M diluted shares, about 3-4% above the $1.50-1.51 consensus; the bar sits barely above Q2's $1.48.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HBCP has beaten EPS consensus six quarters running (MarketBeat). Big beats of 21-23c in 2025 traded +10.66%, +0.62%, +2.37%; the smaller beats since (+7c Q4'25, +6c Q1'26, +2c Q2'26) traded -3.26%, -1.39%, +0.63% (baseline history). Beats of this size have recently been sold or ignored.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $1.50-1.51 is only 2-3c above Q2's $1.48 despite a guided NIM rise and loan growth; if the guide math were priced, estimates would sit near $1.55. But the beat lands inside what the company guided, and this name beats routinely, so most of it is expected by holders. That is why the size is small.
findings.independence: Q2 figures from the 8-K release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001436425/000162828026048827/a2026q2earningsrelease.htm); bar from two estimate pages. The guidance and the arithmetic share one document, the call transcript.

findings.finding: Credit is the swing line. At Q2, criticized loans rose to $95.8M (3.45% of loans), foreclosed assets jumped from $4.1M to $12.8M and NPAs were $39.2M (1.09% of assets). On the call, the President guided to more than $30M of special-asset improvement by year-end, including about $22M of special-mention resolutions with 'more than half in Q3', plus ~$7M of NPA improvement from payoffs, upgrades and OREO sales. Q3 is the first test of that promise; a shortfall or an OREO write-down would land against it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NPAs rose from $25.4M (Q2'25) to $39.9M (Q1'26) over the quarters that traded -3.26% and -1.39%; Q2'26, with NPAs slightly lower but criticized up, traded +0.63%. No clean isolation of the credit line is available.
findings.why_not_priced: Management quantified the resolution path and dated part of it to Q3, so delivery is expected. What is not priced is the variance around it: OREO sale prices and whether new criticized inflows offset the payoffs. Two-sided, so the size is near zero.
findings.independence: The criticized/OREO levels come from the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001436425/000162828026048827/a2026q2earningsrelease.htm); the resolution guide comes from the same call transcript as finding 1, a different line of it.

findings.finding: The peer read-through is benign. Regions (a Southeast regional with Louisiana overlap) reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-16 with NIM up to 3.68%, NII up 1.6% quarter on quarter on lower deposit costs and loan growth, and adjusted EPS $0.73 against ~$0.64-0.66 consensus. Its shares were +2.3% premarket. Northrim's Q3 NII also rose ($35.8M vs $33.2M). The Fed funds rate has been held at 3.75% since December 2025, so the quarter was stable for rates.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No HBCP-specific history on peer read-through; HBCP reports a few days after the large Gulf South regionals each quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: Regions was public three days ago and HBCP did not rally (-0.53% over 5 days). Filed as a proxy. HBCP's CFO said in July he does not expect further material declines in deposit costs, so the transmission is weak.

findings.finding: Short interest roughly tripled this year to 311,849 shares (4.0% of shares outstanding, 4.5 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement), and the stock has slid from $71.68 (an insider's 2026-08-18 sale price) to $65.90, -9% from its 52-week high. A clean print meets a modestly larger short base on a ~57k-share/day float.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior squeeze on a print in the 7-event history; the largest move (+10.66% in April 2025) came in a market-wide rebound.
findings.why_not_priced: 4.5 days to cover in a name trading ~57k shares a day means covering is visible in the price if a beat triggers it. At 4% of shares the short is not crowded, so this is a mild asymmetry, not a mechanism.
findings.independence: Insider sale price from Form 4 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1436425/000143642526000074/form4.xml); the short data is a single aggregator.

findings.finding: There is capital-return room at today's price. 383,170 shares (~4.9% of shares outstanding) remain on the 2025 repurchase plan. Management said in July it had been out of the buyback market 'given the stock's recent run' and would re-evaluate; the stock is now ~$66, about where it bought 2,720 shares in Q2 ($66.19 average), with TBV $47.02 and the sub-debt call in 2027 the stated alternative use of capital.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Buyback commentary has not been a visible driver of HBCP prints; the dividend raise came in July this year, not October, so no raise is expected with this release.
findings.why_not_priced: Q3 buyback activity is disclosed only in the release. A pick-up after the stock fell ~9% from August would be new, but management named M&A as the first use of capital, so the size is small.
findings.independence: Call commentary on buybacks and M&A: https://www.webull.com/news/15267258756637696

searched_and_found_nothing: Hurricane exposure: Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin FL on 2026-10-10 (https://www.wlox.com/2026/10/10/hurricane-isaias-winds-rip-part-roof-off-florida-hotel-during-landfall/; WAFB 2026-10-08 forecast kept Louisiana outside the impact zone, https://www.wafb.com/2026/10/08/hurricane-isaias-make-landfall-friday-night-along-gulf-coast/). It missed HBCP's Acadiana/Baton Rouge/New Orleans/Houston footprint and came after quarter-end. No Louisiana landfall in Q3.

EDGAR since the Q2 print: only the 10-Q (08-03), the date-announcement 8-K (10-05), two small Form 4 option-exercise-and-sell trades by the Chief Banking Officer (800 shares at $69.39 on 07-24; 750 at $71.68 on 08-18) and a Form 3 for a new Chief Risk Officer (Darren M. Hill, 08-17), who succeeds Guidry after Guidry's announced promotion to President. All routine: no 8-K item 5.02 surprise, no M&A, no financing.
Company IR page: no releases between the 07-20 results and the 10-05 date notice.

Louisiana peers Hancock Whitney (HWC) and Investar (ISTR) have not yet reported Q3 2026 (EDGAR shows no Q3 8-K for HWC as of 10-19), so no direct Louisiana counterparty read is available inside the window before HBCP.
Analyst actions since July: nothing dated found; aggregator targets around $73 (August), a SureDividend Hold with a $67 fair value (2026-08-11).
Options: no usable chain in the baseline (no_paired_strikes), so no skew or implied move to read.

rejected_candidates.candidate: A Q3 dividend increase as a catalyst
rejected_candidates.detail: The 2026 dividend raise (3%, to $0.32) was already declared with the Q2 release on 2026-07-20, so the October-raise pattern of 2025 does not carry into this print.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Rising-rate/oil-inflation pressure on regional banks as a negative
rejected_candidates.detail: The page carries no date, so it cannot be placed in 2026; and HBCP's CFO said NIM can be sustained or improved under a hike (call transcript).

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The mild positive lean runs against a soft tape (-3.3% over 20 days, -9% from the high) and against this name's recent habit of fading small beats, so p_up sits only two points above 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a reaction; this name sold its last small beats, -3.26 and -1.39): guide-math beat finding cut from +0.4 to +0.2, and p_up from 53 to 52.
Lesson 6 (a finding inside the guide): credit-resolution finding cut from +0.1 to +0.05, because management dated the resolutions to Q3 itself.
Lesson 5 (proxy and macro transmission): Regions/Northrim read-through cut from +0.2 to +0.1.
Lesson 5/7 (positioning is not evidence by itself; short not crowded at 4%): short-interest finding cut from +0.2 to +0.1.
Left standing: the buyback finding (+0.1), abs_move_pct 2.6 (lesson 8 does not apply because no unpriced confirmed number exists), and print_vs_bar_pct +3.0.
